title: Likelihood and estimators
dek: A model is a family of distributions. The likelihood is that family read as a function of the parameter. Estimation is what you do with that function.
story: Data y are treated as the realized value of a random variable Y ~ f(y | θ). Once y is observed, the same formula, now a function of θ, is the likelihood L(θ | y) = f(y | θ). Nothing mystical happened: you froze the data and unfroze the parameter.

The maximum-likelihood estimator θ̂(y) is a maximizer of L, or equivalently of ℓ = log L. For regular models, ℓ is approximately quadratic near the peak; the curvature is Fisher information; the sampling distribution of θ̂ is approximately Normal with variance I(θ)⁻¹ / n in the iid case.

An estimator is a function of the data. Bias, variance, and consistency are properties of that function under the sampling distribution — they are not properties of a single number you already computed. A good MLE can still look embarrassing in n = 12 with a weakly identified parameter.
deepTitle: The objects you actually write down
deep: For independent observations, L(θ) = ∏ f(yᵢ | θ) and ℓ(θ) = Σ log f(yᵢ | θ). The score S(θ) = ∇ℓ, and the MLE solves S(θ̂) = 0 when the maximum is interior. Observed information is −∇²ℓ(θ̂); expected (Fisher) information is E[−∇²ℓ(θ)].

Invariance: if θ̂ is the MLE of θ, g(θ̂) is the MLE of g(θ). Delta method: √n (g(θ̂) − g(θ)) →d N(0, ∇gᵀ I⁻¹ ∇g). This is how you get a standard error for a transmission probability that was estimated on the logit scale.

Misspecification: if the true distribution is not in {f(·|θ)}, the MLE converges to the Kullback–Leibler projection, not to “the truth.” Sandwich (Huber–White) variance is the adult response. In TB WGS–DST, the catalogue model is misspecified by design; sandwich and hierarchical residuals are not optional garnish.

Bayesian analysis uses the same f(y|θ) as a likelihood and multiplies by a prior. The likelihood function does not change teams. What changes is whether you treat θ as unknown-but-fixed or as a random variable.

example.title: Bernoulli MLE for a FQ-R proportion
example.setup: n = 50 sequenced RR-TB isolates, y = 8 with a high-confidence gyrA QRDR mutation. Model: Yᵢ iid Bernoulli(π). Estimate π and a Wald interval.

steps.title: Write ℓ
steps.body: ℓ(π) = 8 log π + 42 log(1−π), for π ∈ (0,1).

steps.title: Maximize
steps.body: Score 8/π − 42/(1−π) = 0 ⇒ π̂ = 8/50 = 0.16. This is also the sample mean, as it must be in an exponential family with identity mean map.

steps.title: Information and a caution
steps.body: I(π) = n / (π(1−π)). Plug-in SE = √(0.16×0.84/50) ≈ 0.052. A Wald interval 0.16 ± 1.96 SE is a large-sample statement; with 8 events, a score or likelihood-ratio interval is less theatrical near 0.

example.takeaway: Write ℓ, differentiate, state the sampling claim — and notice when nπ is too small for Wald theatre.

check.prompt: After data are observed, the likelihood L(θ | y) is:
choices: The probability that the parameter equals θ
The sampling density viewed as a function of θ with y held fixed
Always a Normal curve in θ
check.answer: The sampling density viewed as a function of θ with y held fixed
check.why: Likelihood is not a probability distribution on θ unless you add a prior and normalize.

whyWrong.The probability that the parameter equal: That would require a prior (or a discrete parameter with a mass function you already believe).
whyWrong.Always a Normal curve in θ: Only a local large-sample approximation in regular models.

check.prompt: iid Poisson(λ), n = 4, data 1, 2, 0, 1. What is the MLE λ̂?
check.why: For Poisson, λ̂ = ȳ = (1+2+0+1)/4 = 1. The likelihood ∏ e^{−λ} λ^{yᵢ}/yᵢ! is maximized at the mean.

whyWrong.0: That would maximize nothing relevant here.
whyWrong.2: That is the maximum observation, not the MLE.
whyWrong.4: That is n, not the mean.

check.prompt: On the density plate, why is a prior curve drawn next to the likelihood?
check.figureHint: Three labeled curves share one θ axis.
choices: Because the prior is the sampling distribution of θ̂
To show that Bayes multiplies the same likelihood by a prior; the likelihood itself does not change teams
Because MLE requires a prior to exist
check.answer: To show that Bayes multiplies the same likelihood by a prior; the likelihood itself does not change teams
check.why: The plate’s point is ontological hygiene: one f(y|θ), two cultures of what you do with θ.

whyWrong.Because the prior is the sampling distri: Sampling laws live on estimates, priors live on parameters.
whyWrong.Because χ² references are priors: They are sampling references under H₀.
